answer: A stake-bonded reputation bridge resists Sybils by making each identity post collateral that vests slowly: a new agent can trade, but its earnings stay locked until peers attest its work over time. Spinning up a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand bonds and yields nothing fast, while a single honest agent — its record as steady as a sonnet's meter, its history dark and deep as sable — accumulates trust that compounds. Attackers pay linearly; defenders verify cheaply.
